member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Core.Connections.ConnectionHealthPolicy
member.summary:
The connection-health state machine (report §6–§7). Pure: it reads the current health and one attempt, and returns the next health and the outcome, which fires only on the transition that earns it.
One success makes any state Healthy; it resolves only a state the user was told about.
A definitive credential failure, a suspect one seen again after , or a suspect one followed by a probe that fails on the credential too, makes any state ActionRequired, which holds until a success.
Any other counted failure makes Healthy Degraded (silent); Failing once there are failures and without a success; Dormant once the streak has lasted .
A rate-limited answer counts like a transient one, is never a credential signal, and may carry the time before which no scheduled run calls the provider ().
A not-ready answer is not counted while the last success is younger than the source's (a connection that never succeeded is aged from when it was connected); past it, it counts like a transient failure.
An internal failure is ours, not the provider's: it leaves the health as it was.
A scheduled run skips an ActionRequired connection (), except for one probe per ; a success clears the state as usual. An active provider's Dormant connection is slowed the same way, to one run per ().
A suspect credential failure, or a Dormant connection, is probed (): a cheap authenticated call per provider, at most one per connection per . A failed probe that is a credential failure confirms the suspicion (); a successful one clears it but never heals a Dormant connection ().

When a scheduled run may next call the provider, or null when it may go ahead now. Two things pause it, and the later wins:
The provider named a time (, a rate limit's Retry-After) that has not come.
The connection is ActionRequired and its probe is not due. The probe is timed from , which a failed probe renews, so no field is added; a connection with no failure on record has nothing to time from and is probed at once. A probe may start early.
With (the provider is in ), a Dormant connection is paused too (). A run the person triggers does not ask: it always goes ahead.

member.summary: When a Dormant connection's slowed cadence next lets a scheduled run try it, or null when it may go ahead now (or is not Dormant): one run per , timed from as the ActionRequired probe is, so a failed run renews the pause and a reconnect that clears the last failure lets the next run through. A success leaves Dormant, so the cadence is back at once. Whether it applies is the caller's: only to a provider in .

A failed probe (): recorded as any failed attempt, except that a credential failure on a connection already suspect confirms it at once - the report's "once plus a failed probe" - whatever its own strength, so the connection becomes ActionRequired without waiting out . Any other failure (an outage, a rate limit) confirms nothing and is counted as usual.

A probe proves the credential works, not that the resource whose failure made the connection Dormant is back, so it only clears the suspicion there; the state, the failure streak and the last failure that times the slowed cadence stay, and only a success of the slowed sync itself () heals it and resolves the alert.

T:FinanceSentry.Core.Measures.CapacityIndicator
member.summary: The capacity indicator (#454 S7): a pure function of how long cash lasts, what is spent against what comes in, how steady the income is and how soon a dated goal falls due. It is a rubric, not a measure: each input caps the band the answer can reach, and the suggestion is the lowest cap, so one weak input holds the suggestion down however strong the others are. Capacity is what the person can afford to lose, as opposed to tolerance, which is what they would sit through; this reads only the former and never infers a tolerance. Context for the owner's own re-measurement, never a trading signal; it produces no buy, sell or hold call. The thresholds are named below and written out in money-semantics §20.

member.name: T:FinanceSentry.Core.Measures.ScopeLinks
member.summary: Rule 3 of finance-framework §3.2 for a scope measured from one aggregate value series: a newly linked account is not growth. A link on day L is seen by the first close after L and maybe by L's own close (the snapshot runs at 01:00 UTC), so the sub-period from the last valued close before L to the first one after it carries the linked value. That stretch becomes one sub-period whose whole change, less its recorded external flows, is a synthetic external flow at its end: its return is exactly zero in M3, its value is capital, not gain, in M4, and M2 names it "newly linked". A link at the window's first close moves the opening to the first close after it; a link at the last close moves the closing back before it. Links outside the window are ignored. The window opens on the first close that holds value: a scope that held nothing yet (closes of zero or none before the first account was linked) has no base, and a later close of zero that no recorded withdrawal explains is dropped (). Market moves inside the bridged stretch are lost into the linked line, a day or two at most. Pure: no I/O, no clock.
